# IEEE binary64 TIFF input references

432 synthetic inputs generated by `../generate_tiff_double.py` with NumPy
float64 and tifffile, pinned by SHA-256. Gray/RGB, alpha association, planar
layout, white gray, byte order, classic/BigTIFF, Deflate, orientation and three
ICC choices follow the binary16 matrix. Data includes float32 maximum, minimum
normal/subnormal and smaller values, signed zero, HDR, nextafter(1,2), and 1/3
alpha. RGB matrix-profile samples stay within the converted float32 range.

`../verify_tiff_half.py --bits 64` independently decodes actual float64 values,
performs inversion/division before float32 rounding, then checks ICC results,
project CRC/metadata, TIFF and EXR output bits. This checks explicit conversion
to the app's float32 layers; it does not claim native float64 editing or output.
Subnormal underflow and associated storage rounding are reflected in the oracle.
